definition: The number of requests, tokens, or predictions a system can process per unit of time.
details: Throughput and latency often trade off against each other; systems can be tuned (e.g., via batching) to prioritize one over the other depending on the application's requirements.
story: Picture a librarian organizing a million slips of paper so that any one of them can be found in a heartbeat. Think of it this way: The number of requests, tokens, or predictions a system can process per unit of time. And here is the clever part: Throughput and latency often trade off against each other; systems can be tuned (e.g., via batching) to prioritize one over the other depending on the application's requirements. Garbage in, garbage out — and the reverse: clean, representative data makes the model quietly brilliant. And that is Throughput — the unglamorous work everything else stands on.
